title: Every Other Item
statement:
Walk through a list two steps at a time and keep only the items you land on.

The first line is a whole number `n`. The second line holds `n` integers separated by single spaces. `n` is at least 1. Print the items at indexes 0, 2, 4, and so on, in their original order, on one line separated by single spaces. When the list has one item, print just that item.

Input:

```text
6
10 20 30 40 50 60
```

Expected output:

```text
10 30 50
```
hints: Index 0 is the first item, so the first item is always printed.
A counting loop does not have to go up by 1. Let it go up by 2 instead.

python.solution:
def every_other(items: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    result = []
    for i in range(0, len(items), 2):
        result.append(items[i])
    return result


n = int(input())
items = [int(x) for x in input().split()]
print(" ".join(str(x) for x in every_other(items)))
